title: The card that outstayed its welcome
text: {{1}} centuries, the exchange of printed cards opened working relationships across the world. The card was proof {{2}} the holder was genuine, and the little rectangle was handled with more care than most documents. In the West the smartphone has largely swept it aside, and contact details now travel {{3}} one phone to another. {{4}}, in Japan the meishi survives: it is presented {{5}} both hands and a small bow, received with a nod, studied carefully and then tucked respectfully into a wallet, and treating {{6}} carelessly is a genuine insult. The ritual looks quaint, yet it encodes something universal: a relationship deserves a moment of ceremony, {{7}} brief the encounter. It remains to be seen {{8}} the rest of the world will decide the ceremony was worth keeping.
